spots.cost: No extra toll — same Rifugio Auronzo car park as Tre Cime (€40/car, one timed slot covers both). The viewpoint hike itself is free: ~3.9km out-and-back, ~1hr, only 144m of gain on path #117.
spots.climate: Easy hike, one exposed catch. Short and mostly gentle from the car park — but the famous photo promontory is a narrow ridge with cliff drop-offs. Doable with kids if you keep the 8-year-old close and stop short of the knife-edge tip; the 13-year-old is fine with care in dry weather. A right-side contour path skips the exposed crest entirely. Skip it if wet, icy, or windy.
spots.saveHtml: Save This is the rare free epic — no lift, no separate ticket. Do it first, at sunrise, before the Tre Cime loop while the light rakes the needles and the ridge is empty, then walk back to the car and start the big loop.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a local sunrise photo guide from Misurina — they know exactly where the family can stand safely for the postcard frame and handle the pre-dawn timing so you don't.
spots.restoHtml:

  • Lakeside at Lago di Misurina — pizza and gelato by the lake at the foot of the toll road
spots.altboxHtml:

• Lu Fanali — Stintino lungomare pizzeria/bar facing the harbor; pizza and big-portion pasta
  • Il Gabbiano — beachfront terrace; plain pizza while the kids play on the sand steps away
  • Il Portico — Lungomare Colombo; standard kids’ pizza and pasta menu
spots.altboxHtml:
• Asinara National Park — a former-penal-colony island by ferry from Stintino, a full nature/wildlife day.
  • Spiaggia delle Saline — a longer, less-regulated Stintino beach if La Pelosa is capped out.
  • Skip the drive — trade La Pelosa for a second Costa Smeralda day if nobody wants the road time.

days.heading: South to the Gulf of Orosei

facts.label: Afternoon
facts.valueHtml: Settle, town beach or Cala Fuili

days.note: A scenic drive down the east coast to the trip’s final base, tucked under the Supramonte cliffs. Keep the afternoon easy — the free town beach or pebbly Cala Fuili — and rest legs before the two big east-coast days.

spots.name: Cala Gonone & Grotta del Bue Marino

spots.cost: Town beach free. Cave + Cala Luna boat trip ~€90–130/family; short cave-only from €15/person + cave entry & €2 eco tax.
spots.climate: 86°F day / 69°F night. Sea ~75°F — clear and calm in the harbor, sheltered from the Maestrale wind.
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip the boat and walk the free Spiaggia Centrale plus a short stroll to pebbly Cala Fuili — a rest morning for ~€0–20 before the big Orosei boat day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A private cave + Cala Luna + snorkel combo charter (~€250–300/family) with a small operator — sea cave, beach, and swimming stops at your own pace.
spots.restoHtml:
• La Favorita Pizzeria Bistrot — waterfront, seafood + wood-fired pizza; plain margherita for the kids
  • Ristorante Il Banjo — seafront promenade trattoria/pizzeria; kids’ pasta al pomodoro
  • Pizzeria Zio Pedrillo — casual two-level pizzeria, margherita €7, gluten-free available
spots.altboxHtml:
• Cala Fuili — white pebbles and turquoise water a short drive/walk from town, the free rest-morning option.
  • Grotta del Bue Marino — a short sea-cave boat trip when you want an easy on-the-water outing.
  • Dorgali town — a low-key craft-and-gelato stroll 10 minutes inland.

days.heading: Cala Goloritzé & the Orosei coves
days.note: The climax: a full-day boat along the Gulf of Orosei to the most-photographed cove in Italy — Cala Goloritzé, its limestone pinnacle over water so clear the boats look like they float on air. Cala Luna and Mariolu on the way. This is the shot the trip was built around.

spots.name: Gulf of Orosei Boat Day — Cala Goloritzé
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · calagoloritzeIG · golfodioroseiIG · sardiniaFlickr

images.alt: Cala Goloritzé pinnacle and turquoise cove

spots.cost: Full-day group boat from Cala Gonone ~€55–70 adult / €35 child — ~€190–210/family + €2/person eco tax. Most groups moor off Goloritzé (swim-up), not land.
spots.climate: 86°F day / 69°F night. Sea ~75°F — the sheltered Orosei gulf is turquoise, clear, and calm; the reason this is the finale.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take the standard group boat (~€200/family) doing the Luna–Mariolu–Goloritzé circuit rather than a private charter — same coves, several hundred euros less.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A private full-day skipper charter (~€650) — land where you like, linger at Cala Mariolu, and reach Goloritzé’s arch without a fixed timetable.
spots.restoHtml:
• La Favorita Pizzeria Bistrot — Cala Gonone waterfront, the reliable post-boat pizza dinner
  • Ristorante Il Banjo — seafront pasta and pizza a short walk from the harbor
  • Pizzeria Zio Pedrillo — the easy kid-pleaser after a long day on the water
spots.altboxHtml:
• Cala Mariolu — the white-pebble, ultra-clear cove usually on the same boat itinerary; the swim stop that steals the day.
  • Cala Luna — the wide crescent with sea caves, a common lunch anchorage on the route.
  • Santa Maria Navarrese — an alternate boat launch to the south if Cala Gonone is booked out.

days.heading: Su Gorropu, or a well-earned beach
days.note: A flexible last full day. The strong-legged can tackle Su Gorropu — Europe’s deepest gorge — via the gentle Flumineddu valley approach, starting at dawn to beat the July heat and turning back before the hardest sections with the 8-year-old. Or just claim a final beach.

spots.name: Su Gorropu Gorge (Flumineddu Valley)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · sugorropuIG · gorropuIG · supramonteFlickr

images.alt: River through the Flumineddu valley
images.captionTitle: River through the Flumineddu valley

images.alt: Mountain stream in a rocky green valley
images.captionTitle: Mountain stream in a rocky green valley

spots.cost: Self-guided entry €5 adult / €3.50 child (~€17/family, cash). Guided 4×4 + hike ~€55 adult / €45 child (~€200/family).
spots.climate: Low 90s°F in the open valley by midday, cooler (~75–80°F) deep in the shaded gorge — start by 7–8am; several guides call July midday “too hot.”
spots.saveHtml: Save Go self-guided from the Sa Barva Bridge with your own car and water (~€17 entry) rather than booking a guided tour — the valley approach is well-trodden and needs no rope work.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A private guided 4×4 + hike (~€200) — a licensed guide, the bumpy transfer to the trailhead, and a safer margin with an 8-year-old near the gorge’s harder sections.
spots.restoHtml:
• La Favorita Pizzeria Bistrot — 10 minutes from Dorgali on the Cala Gonone waterfront, a big carb reload
  • Ristorante Il Banjo — seafront pasta and pizza, the easy picky-eater dinner
  • Pizzeria Zio Pedrillo — casual, margherita and gluten-free for tired kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Cala Fuili rest afternoon — pair the hard gorge morning with an easy beach, not a second activity.
  • Tiscali nuraghic village — a shorter archaeological hike in the same Supramonte if the heat is brutal.
  • Swap it entirely — a lazy last beach day is a legitimate choice on a trip this full.

days.note: An easy last drive back up to Olbia, drop the second car, and fly home — landing in Pittsburgh the same day. A Sunday return means no PTO spent getting home; the memory card is full.

Both legal windows cost about the same PTO because both slot a federal holiday mid-trip. The June 27 window wins on details: both travel days fall on a weekend (depart Sunday evening, land home Sunday), so no PTO is burned traveling. Travel Tips

The stuff nobody tells you

Researched July 2026 for June-July 2027. Book in roughly this order; the first three are the ones that actually run out.

Book in roughly this order

  1. Transatlantic open-jaw flights · by Dec 2026 for the low band
  2. All four lodging bases · Jan-Feb 2027, apartments first
  3. VCE->OLB Volotea flight + bags · once dates are firm
  4. Tre Cime toll slot + Lago di Braies car reservation · when they open
  5. La Maddalena & Orosei boats, La Pelosa ticket · 1-2 months out in peak July

  • Driving

    Permits and the fines nobody warns you about

    • Get an IDP from AAA before you fly. Italian desks check for it and you cannot get one in-country.
    • Cortina has a camera-enforced ZTL. Register your plate with the hotel.
    • Time the first car pickup for Venice departure day (Jun 30), not arrival — you don’t need a car in Venice.

  • Pre-booked sites

    Three Dolomite spots now need slots

    • Tre Cime toll road: €40/car with a mandatory timed slot at auronzo.info.
    • Lago di Braies: valley closed to cars 9am-4pm from July 1; reserve at prags.bz.
    • Seceda cableway: timed-slot pre-booking in summer; buy one-way up if hiking down.

  • Beach logistics

    Sardinia’s booked and banned beaches

    • La Pelosa is ticketed: €3.50/person, capped 1,500/day, released in two waves.
    • You can’t land on Spiaggia Rosa — boats idle offshore; swim at Cala Corsara.
    • Mornings are calm and clear — wind and crowds build after midday.

  • Money & food

    Cash, eSIM, picky kids

    • Carry euro cash for the Tre Cime toll, rifugi, and boat eco-taxes — cards aren’t universal.
    • Every stop has a margherita — rifugi do pasta/polenta/fries, pizzerias do €7 pizzas.
    • A cheap EU eSIM covers Venice, the Dolomites, and Sardinia on one plan.

Pre-Departure To-Do

What to do when

Updated July 2026: deadlines separate tracking, refundable holds, and real booking windows so the list does not create false urgency a year out.

blocks.title: Track, do not panic-buy
blocks.note: Inventory opening is a search-alert trigger, not a cash-fare deadline.
items: Set fare alerts for the protected routing plus one acceptable fallback airport/routing.
Do not buy cash airfare just because seats opened; only grab award space or a fare already inside the trip budget with good flight times.
Track Venice/Milan/Bologna plus Sardinia exit options; the protected air chain matters more than buying the first fare.

blocks.title: Hold scarce refundable stays
blocks.note: This is about protecting scarce family inventory, not chasing prepaid discounts.
items: Hold refundable Dolomites family lodging near the exact hiking base first; July mountain rooms with parking and kid-friendly layouts go early.
Hold refundable Sardinia beach lodging once the island airports and sequence are credible.

blocks.title: Cars, ferries, and route anchors
blocks.note: Use cancellable/pay-later terms where possible, then re-shop after flights are purchased.
items: Reserve cancellable automatic cars for both mainland and Sardinia if needed; re-shop after flights are bought.
Confirm any domestic Italy flight/ferry bridge before making either base nonrefundable.

blocks.title: Buy flights in the real window
blocks.note: For peak-summer Europe, this is the practical cash-buy window: Google Flights puts U.S.-Europe fares near 94 days out, while Going gives 2-8 months for international trips and says to shift earlier for peak periods.
items: Buy when the total family fare and schedule both work; waiting for a theoretical bottom is not worth bad layovers or split seats.

blocks.title: Timed tickets and tours
blocks.note: These are the tasks with real external release windows or limited capacity.
items: Tre Cime shuttle/road access requires online reservation/payment in the summer system; watch 2027 release timing (Drei Zinnen).
Lago di Braies summer access uses online day-stay/parking controls after the unrestricted early-season period; check the 2027 dates (Prags Parking).
Cala Goloritze opens 72 hours before visit and caps access, so set the reminder after the Sardinia day is fixed (Costa di Baunei).

blocks.title: Final checks
items: Passports: Schengen requires validity 3+ months after planned EU departure and issue within the last 10 years (EU); renew before winter if anyone is close.
ETIAS: no July 2026 action; the U.S. State Dept. says ETIAS is planned for late 2026, so apply only after the official system launches (State Dept.).
Insurance: compare family medical/trip coverage after the first meaningful deposit; waiver timing is policy-specific, so do not wait until final payment if coverage matters.
Re-check Dolomites trail/snow conditions and Sardinia beach access rules during the final two weeks.
